packs.name: Budget Tracker
packs.summary: A row per transaction, a monthly limit per category, a calendar of bills; month-by-month charts summed from the rows.
packs.description: Three small databases that stay filled in. `budget` is the ledger: one row per transaction with a date, an amount, a kind (expense, income, transfer), a category and an account. `budget-limits` holds one row per category with the monthly amount you mean to spend; open a limit and its page charts what you actually spent, month by month, under it. `budget-bills` is every recurring charge with its cycle and next due date, on a calendar, and each bill's page lists the payments you logged against it. The ledger's own views chart income against spending per month and each category over time — all summed from the rows when you open them, nothing to update by hand.
packs.credits: The transactions / limits / bills split and the budget-versus-actual page follow the budget trackers in Notion's gallery (Easlo, Thomas Frank, Matthias Frank) and the envelope spreadsheets they copy; the charts-on-read design is our own.

packs.name: Contacts
packs.summary: People with a keep-in-touch cadence and a log of every conversation: who to reach out to, follow-ups, history.
packs.description: A personal CRM in two databases. Contacts is one row per person: how you know them, how often you mean to be in touch (monthly, quarterly, twice a year…), when you last spoke and when to reach out next, plus company, role, birthday, and a page for how you met and what to remember. Interactions is one row per conversation — date, who, what kind, one line of summary — and every person's page embeds their own history from it. The Reach out view sorts people by longest silence first, the Follow-ups calendar turns next-contact dates into a schedule, and the month chart shows whether you are actually keeping in touch.
packs.credits: The keep-in-touch cadence comes from Dex and the tiered personal CRMs in Notion's gallery (Circles of Trust); the one-file-per-interaction log and the person page that lists its own meetings come from Dann Berg's Obsidian people template and the obsidian-personal-crm plugin.

packs.name: Content Calendar
packs.summary: Every piece of content from idea to published: pipeline board, publish calendar, a queue, campaigns, a monthly chart.
packs.description: One row per piece of content — the row is the draft. `status` carries it from idea through drafting, review and scheduled to published; `channel` and `format` say where and what; `due` is the draft deadline and `publish` the day it goes out. The Pipeline board is the flow, the Calendar is the month, the Queue is what is next in publish order, Ideas is the inbox, and a bar chart counts what actually shipped per month, one bar per channel. Campaigns are a second collection: a launch or a series with its own page that shows its pieces as a live board. Each piece's page carries a brief, an outline, the draft, a publish checklist and a table of what was repurposed from it.
packs.credits: Shaped by the content and editorial calendars in Notion's gallery (Notion's own Content Calendar and Social Media Calendar, Easlo's Content Calendar, Thomas Frank's Creator's Companion) and by Bases-driven calendars in the Obsidian community.

packs.name: Daily Note
packs.summary: One page per day with mood, energy and sleep: a calendar of the days you wrote, weekly trend charts, a running log.
packs.description: A journal as a database: every day is one row with a `mood`, an `energy` and `sleep` number, the areas it touched and a one-line highlight, plus a page whose body is the day — an intention and three priorities in the morning, a timestamped log as you go, a short evening reflection. The calendar shows the days you wrote (and the gaps); the Energy and Sleep charts average each week so a bad month is visible before you feel it; the Moods chart counts how the year has felt. New row gives you today in one keystroke, already titled with the date. Pairs with Weekly Review (read the week's pages before you review it) and Habit Tracker (habits stay in their own log).
packs.credits: Mood, energy and sleep as properties with a calendar and weekly trend charts is the shape of the best-rated daily journals in Notion's gallery (Eve Jiyū's Daily Reflection Journal, mrpugo's Energy Journal, Easlo's minimal journal); the morning-intention / log / evening-highlight body follows the Obsidian daily-note templates of Sébastien Dubois and Vault of Josh.

packs.name: Decision Log
packs.summary: One row per decision: context, options, what was chosen and why, a review date, and later the outcome you got.
packs.description: A decisions database rather than a loose note. Each row carries `status` (proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded), the date it was `decided`, a `review` date, an `area`, its `impact` and whether it is `reversible`, your `confidence` at the time and, once you have looked back, the `outcome`. The row's page is the record: context and state of mind, the options with their good and bad points, the decision and the one reason that carried it, what you expect to happen, the consequences, and a review section you fill in on the review date. A `supersedes` relation links a new decision to the one it replaces, and the old page shows what superseded it. Views: Log, Board by status, Due for review, a calendar of review dates and a chart of outcomes by month. Works for a team's architecture decisions and for one person's life ones.
packs.credits: Architecture decision records (Michael Nygard; the MADR template), Farnam Street's decision journal, and the decision databases in Notion's gallery that add a review date and an outcome.

packs.name: Goals
packs.summary: Goals with milestones and dated check-ins; each goal's page charts its own progress, the board shows which are drifting.
packs.description: Three databases. `goals` is one row per goal with its life area, timeframe (year, quarter, month), priority, start and target dates, a one-line measure of done, and a status that says planned, on track, at risk, off track, done or dropped. `goal-milestones` breaks a goal into dated steps with their own status board and calendar. `goal-checkins` is the review log: one short row per check-in with the date, the progress number and your confidence, so progress is a line over time instead of a number you overwrite. Open a goal and its page lists its milestones, charts its check-ins and keeps the why, the plan and the obstacles under them.
packs.credits: Goals / milestones / check-ins follows the goal trackers in Notion's gallery (Benny Builds It, Jithin Rajiv, Easlo, Thomas Frank's Ultimate Brain) and the OKR check-in habit; the per-goal progress chart is our own.

packs.name: Habit Tracker
packs.summary: Habits as rows, one file per day; streaks, day scores and a year heatmap computed on read, never stored.
packs.description: Each habit is a row with its own page; each day is one small file whose `done:` list names what you did. Tick today in the Today view (Space on a habit, or `mod+shift+h` for "Log today…" from anywhere), and the week grid, month, and year heatmap fill in on their own — current and longest streaks, perfect days, completion — all computed from the files, so nothing is ever reset and nothing goes stale. A day with no file is a day with nothing done; the first tick creates it. Pair it with `templates/daily-with-habits.md` as your daily note so today's habits sit at the top of your journal.
packs.credits: The streak, heatmap and week-grid ideas come from the habit trackers in Notion's gallery; the day-file model is our own so history is never reset.

packs.name: Meeting Notes
packs.summary: Meetings as rows with date, kind, status and attendees; action items in their own list, linked to the meeting.
packs.description: One row per meeting in `collections/meetings/`: when, what kind, who was there, a one-line summary, and a status that moves from scheduled to held to followed-up. Open a meeting and the page has the shape a note needs a month later — agenda, notes, decisions, action items, open questions — with a live table of that meeting's action items at the bottom. Action items are rows of their own in `collections/action-items/` with an owner, a due date and a status, so "what is still open from last week's meetings" is a view, not a search. Views: All (newest first), Upcoming, Calendar, a board by status for follow-up, and a chart of meetings per week by kind.
packs.credits: The properties and views follow the most-used meeting-notes databases in Notion's gallery and Dann Berg's meeting template for Obsidian; the separate action-items list is the advice that comes up in every review of them.

packs.name: 1:1 Notes
packs.summary: A page per person with a running agenda, one row per 1:1, and the follow-ups from all of them in one list.
packs.description: Three small databases that fit together. `collections/people/` is one page per person you meet regularly: role, cadence, current focus, a topics list that carries from one meeting to the next, and live tables of their 1:1s and open follow-ups. `collections/one-on-ones/` is one row per meeting — date, person, mood, one-line summary — with a page shaped for the conversation: their topics, yours, since last time, wins, blockers, growth, feedback, follow-ups. `collections/follow-ups/` holds what each of you promised, with an owner and a due date, so what you owe and what you are owed are two views rather than a search. Charts on the 1:1s page count meetings per week by mood and per month by person.
packs.credits: Sections follow Notion's own one-on-one template (past week, this week, blockers, action items) and Dann Berg's people-note pattern for Obsidian; the person page as the durable record with per-meeting notes underneath is the shape every manager's guide converges on.

packs.name: PARA Index
packs.summary: Projects, Areas and Resources as three linked databases; archive is a status, and an index note shows it all live.
packs.description: The PARA method as databases instead of folders. Areas are the ongoing responsibilities (Health, Finances, Career) with a standard to keep and a review date; Projects have an outcome, a deadline and the area they serve; Resources are the articles, books and tools you keep, tied to the area or project they are for. Nothing is ever moved to an Archive folder — a project is `done` or `dropped`, an area or resource is `archived`, and the Archive views filter on that, so relations and history survive. Each area's page lists its own active projects and resources; each project's page lists its resources and next actions. The `Second Brain` note template is the one-page index: active projects, areas, recent resources and the archive, all live.
packs.credits: The PARA method by Tiago Forte (Building a Second Brain). Archive-as-a-status and the area page that lists its own projects and resources come from the PARA templates in Notion's gallery, notably Thomas Frank's and Notion Mastery's.

packs.name: Project Tracker
packs.summary: Projects with status, priority, area, deadline, progress and one next action; milestones on a calendar; a page each.
packs.description: One row per project, and a second small collection of milestones — the dated steps a project is made of. A project has a status (planned / active / on_hold / done / dropped), a priority, an `area`, `start` and `deadline` dates, a `completed` date, a `progress` percentage you set, and one `next_action` so a stalled project is obvious. Views: Open (what is live, p1 first), Board by status, Deadlines on a calendar, Stalled (active projects with no next action) and Finished per month. Each project's page states the outcome, embeds its own milestones, and — if the Tasks pack is installed — a board of the tasks that name it. Milestones have their own calendar, so every key date across every project is on one page.
packs.credits: Follows the project databases in Notion's gallery (Notion's Projects & Tasks, Thomas Frank's Ultimate Brain projects, Easlo's Project Tracker); the single next action is from Getting Things Done.

packs.name: Reading List
packs.summary: Books, articles and papers as rows with a note each; an optional log of sittings adds a heatmap and pages per week.
packs.description: One row per thing you read — book, ebook, audiobook, article or paper — with author, status, format, genre, rating, page count and progress, who recommended it and when you started and finished. The row's page is the reading note: why you picked it up, the ideas, the quotes, the verdict. A second collection, `reading-log`, holds one small row per sitting (date, book, pages); from those the Reading list draws a week grid of what you are reading, a year heatmap on each book's page and a pages-per-week chart, and the Finished view and per-month chart show how the year is going. The log is optional — the list works without it.
packs.credits: Shaped by the reading trackers in Notion's gallery (Thomas Frank's Books, the Bookworm and Book Tracker templates) and by the Obsidian book-tracking write-ups that keep a list of read dates per book.

packs.name: Recipe Box
packs.summary: Recipes as a cookbook gallery, a meal plan on a calendar and a grocery list by aisle; each recipe shows its cook log.
packs.description: Three collections that work as one kitchen. Recipes carry course, cuisine, main ingredient, diet, difficulty, prep and cook minutes, servings, rating, status and source; the ingredients are a checklist and the method a numbered list in the body, and the page ends with a live cook log. Meals are one row per planned meal — a date, a slot, a recipe — so the calendar is your week and a bar chart counts what you actually cooked. Groceries are items with an aisle and a `bought` box: the To buy table is the shopping list, the board is the shop in aisle order.
packs.credits: The recipe, meal-plan and grocery trio follows the recipe managers in Notion's gallery (Matthias Frank's meal planner, the Ultimate Home Chef dashboard, the Frugal and Thriving recipe database) and the Recipe Box and Recipe View plugins for Obsidian.

packs.name: Tasks
packs.summary: One row per task with status, priority, due date and a Today flag; Inbox, Today, Upcoming, a board and a done chart.
packs.description: The task list most people end up building, done once. Each task is a row with a status (todo / doing / waiting / someday / done), a priority (p1–p3), a `due` date, a `today` checkbox for the short list you actually work from, an `area` and a free-text `project`. The views are the ones to-do apps ship: Inbox for what you captured and have not planned, Today, Upcoming by due date, a board by status, and a chart of tasks finished per week. Each task's page has a "done when" line, a checklist of steps and room for notes. Name the same project in the Project Tracker pack and its page shows these tasks.
packs.credits: Properties and views follow the task databases in Notion's gallery (Notion's Projects & Tasks, Thomas Frank's Ultimate Tasks, Easlo's Task Tracker) and the due and done dates of the Obsidian Tasks plugin.

packs.name: Weekly Review
packs.summary: One row per week: Monday plan, Friday review with the get-clear / get-current checklist; rating and carry-over charted.
packs.description: A weekly review as a database. Each week is a row with a `status` (planned, reviewed, skipped), a `rating` out of ten, a one-line `focus`, the `areas` it touched and a `carried_over` count of what slipped. The page has two halves: a Monday plan (focus and Top 3) and a review — the Getting Things Done checklist (get clear, get current), then wins, what slipped, lessons, what gave and drained energy, the carried-over list, and next week's three. A board shows which weeks are still unreviewed, a calendar puts each review on its Monday, and two charts plot the rating and the carry-over count week by week, so a slow decline or a growing backlog is visible. Pairs with Daily Note (read the week's pages first).
packs.credits: The get-clear / get-current / get-creative checklist is David Allen's Weekly Review from Getting Things Done. Weeks as rated rows with monthly trends follows the weekly review databases in Notion's gallery (Thomas Cerulis, Sharky Progress, Simone Smerilli); the plan-then-review page with a carried-over list is the shape of the Vaultorial and Pensio weekly notes for Obsidian; the wins / slipped / energy prompts follow Michelle Mac's.
